title: Non-enzymatic electrochemical urea sensor with Ni-based nanostructures for wastewater monitoring
content: Urea is a major nitrogen pollutant in wastewater, contributing to eutrophication and ecosystem imbalance. Current enzymatic detection methods, while selective, are hindered by poor stability and high operational costs in complex matrices. Here, we present a simple, one-pot synthesis of nickel-based nanostructures for the development of non-enzymatic electrochemical sensors for urea monitoring. The mild chemical reduction strategy produces nanostructures with a narrow distribution of hydrodynamic sizes without the need for autoclaves or complex instrumentation, supporting scalability and cost-effectiveness. The nanostructures were deposited onto carbon-based electrodes, enabling in situ formation of the catalytically active NiOOH phase and amperometric urea sensing. The resulting sensor exhibited a wide linear range (90–2000 µM) and a low detection limit (LoD = 26.9 µM), well suited to real-world monitoring needs. Validation against a commercial colorimetric kit in a certified urine reference material and in municipal wastewater samples supported the reliability of these sensors, with recoveries falling within the accepted analytical window. This approach offers a portable and low-cost alternative to conventional enzymatic assays, opening new perspectives for on-site nitrogen pollution monitoring.
